economy.summary: His campaign platform says he is committed to paying every Pennsylvanian a family-sustaining wage, investing in affordable, high-quality childcare so parents can work, and strengthening unions by making it easier for workers to organize.
economy.short: Supports family-sustaining wages, childcare investment, and stronger unions.

taxes.summary: His campaign platform proposes that the state help municipalities preserve services without increasing local taxes, and give municipalities tools to address rising pension costs he attributes to outdated legislation.
taxes.short: Proposes state help so municipalities avoid raising local taxes.

abortion.summary: In December 2025 he voted for House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment to the Pennsylvania Constitution providing for personal reproductive liberty, which passed the House 102-101.
abortion.short: Voted for reproductive-liberty amendment to the state constitution.

education.summary: His campaign platform calls for increased funding for pre-kindergarten access and support for career and technical education options, saying a child's zip code should not determine their success in school.
education.short: Supports increased pre-K funding and career-technical education options.

healthcare.summary: His campaign platform calls for making health insurance more accessible and affordable and addressing prescription drug costs; he cites his daughter's Type 1 diabetes and the price of insulin as a personal reason for the priority.
healthcare.short: Supports more accessible insurance and lower prescription drug costs.

energy.summary: His campaign platform describes climate change as a long-term threat and says he will work to address warming trends and extreme weather; it also calls for stormwater management systems and keeping rivers and streams clean.
energy.short: Platform calls for climate action and clean rivers and streams.

guns.summary: In May 2023 he voted for final passage of House Bill 714, which would expand background check requirements to include private sales of long guns; the bill passed the House 109-92.
guns.short: Voted to expand background checks to private long-gun sales.
